summary: Iteration 5 — Audio Studio (Read Aloud + Audiobook MP3). Full backend pytest suite (11/11) + Playwright UI flow all passed. Real OpenAI TTS via Emergent universal key works end-to-end. 9 voices catalog, preview MP3 generation, full-doc audiobook download, error/edge cases (auth, validation, ownership, voice fallback, speed clamping) all behave as specified.
critical_code_review_comments: Audiobook endpoint catches ValueError and returns 413 — fine for oversized manuscripts but slightly misleading for empty manuscripts (also raises ValueError). Consider differentiating: empty -> 400, too-large -> 413.
narrate_audiobook chunks are awaited sequentially; for long manuscripts a small concurrency (e.g. asyncio.gather with semaphore) would cut wall time significantly. Not blocking, just performance.
EditorPage.js (1235 lines) approaches the 700-line guideline ceiling; consider extracting Audio Studio + AI Editorial panels into their own components for maintainability.
playTtsPreview uses 'content' (HTML) — correct path. Note: if document is empty the API returns 400 with 'No text to narrate' which surfaces correctly in toast.
test_credentials: Fresh users registered per-run with TEST_ prefix; no shared seed credentials needed. EMERGENT_LLM_KEY confirmed present in /app/backend/.env.
seed_data_creation: Per-test ephemeral users + documents prefixed TEST_ via API (auth/register + documents POST). No production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Audio Studio is fully wired. Backend pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_audio_studio.py covers voices catalog (9), preview happy/error paths, audiobook happy + 401/404/413/voice-fallback/speed-clamp. UI flow validated with Playwright: panel renders, slider updates speed text, Read Aloud spawns blob-URL audio player, Generate Audiobook triggers .mp3 download and shows voice+speed toast. Real OpenAI TTS calls — each preview ~$0.0001. For future iterations, keep audiobook tests on SHORT docs (single chunk) to control cost.
